questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner and about to cross in front of you. What should you do before turning right?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and showers do not speed this up.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always use caution near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices used in work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see these warning signs.

questions.question: When must you obey school crossing guards?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools and always follow their directions.

questions.question: What should you do when a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing?

options.text: You must always give them the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to yield if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use guide dogs or white canes. Always give them the right-of-way no matter where they are crossing.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to turn safely.

questions.question: What is the best way to change lanes?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Change lanes only when needed. Every lane change raises the risk of an accident.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers if you become tired. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes driving dangerous.

questions.question: This is the shape and color of a ____ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle means yield. Slow down to a safe speed and stop if needed. Stop at a marked line if one exists.

questions.question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection. Wait until they cross before proceeding.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Eating and drinking cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down on wet or icy roads. Your tires will not grip as well, so you need to drive slower.

questions.question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, look for both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Only then is it safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving over the speed limit or driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Scanning the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving over the speed limit or driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a common cause of traffic crashes. Always drive at or below the speed limit and adjust your speed for road conditions.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.
questions.explanation: You must stop and stay stopped when a school bus has flashing red lights. Keep stopped until the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas. Let the car slow down. Brake lightly when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed a lot.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention to other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal before you change lanes. Always check your mirrors and turn your head to see your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause crashes that result in damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Honk and keep going at the same speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would behind a regular car.
Follow farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Drive to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind a truck than a regular car because trucks have larger blind spots.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane with no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you, then go.
Drive carefully around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even without a marked crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way in the road.

questions.question: If you drive under the influence and cause a crash that kills someone, you may:

options.text: Be charged with vehicular homicide.
Be fined and sent to prison.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence and causing a death means you can be charged with vehicular homicide. This conviction can result in fines and prison time.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your car—to the sides, ahead, and behind. A good driver knows what is happening everywhere around their vehicle.
